{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e‑business Hosting Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the hosting agreement (document reference: 3.1 Term) 
**Status:** 18 rules assessed — 3 critical deviations, 5 high, 8 medium, 2 low; 6 rules compliant; 2 rules missing

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is workable, and several rules land at or above our preferred position without any redline: there is no exclusivity or non‑compete binding us (§ 14.16 Freedom of Action), no MFN or pricing‑parity obligation (§ 4.1), no minimum purchase or take‑or‑pay commitment (§ 4.1), no non‑solicitation restriction on our hiring (§ 14.8), and no usage or fee audit right against us (§ 11.3 is acceptable‑use enforcement only). Our convenience‑termination right at one month's notice (§ 3.4) and IBM's IP indemnity (§ 8.1, carved out of IBM's cap by § 9.1(a)) are both favourable and we are not opening them.

The risk is concentrated in five areas. First, § 8.2(a)(3) makes us indemnify IBM, uncapped (§ 9.2(a)), for any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" — an open‑ended indemnity for IBM's own Services and, on our playbook, walk‑away territory. Second, § 7 defaults deliverables to IBM‑owned Type II Materials with a licence back that excludes modification and sublicensing, and nothing in the Agreement confirms that we retain rights in our Content or data. Third, although the § 9.1/9.2 caps are mutual and sit at the fallback on amount, there are no carve‑outs for confidentiality, data or wilful misconduct, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes all liability for loss of or damage to our records and data. Fourth, our exit is priced by an open cross‑reference: § 3.4(b) early termination charges are uncapped and undefined in the reviewed text. Fifth, the Agreement is silent on post‑termination transition assistance and Content return (§ 3.5 covers accrued payments only) and contains no insurance obligation at all, notwithstanding that IBM hosts our environment and processes personal information on our behalf.

The balance of the deviations are narrow, single‑sentence fixes: mutual assignment (§ 14.10), removal of IBM's at‑will revocation right in the § 12.1 licence, a 12‑month renewal term with a 30‑day opt‑out (§ 3.2), a 90‑day conformance warranty carved out of the § 5.4(c) "AS IS" disclaimer, and the addition of exclusive New York County venue to the already‑acceptable New York choice of law (§ 14.3).

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / ask |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.2 Indemnification by Customer | IBM's IP indemnity (§ 8.1) sits at or above the fallback and is not redlined. Our indemnity in § 8.2(a)(3) is open‑ended and excluded from our cap by § 9.2(a); narrow it to Customer Content and our breach of applicable law by deleting the Services Recipient limb. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (ownership regime at § 7) | Type II is the default and the licence back omits modification and sublicensing; no confirmation of our Content/data rights (§ 14.17 grants only express licences). Flip the default to Type I, broaden the Type II licence, and add a Customer Content/data ownership sentence. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL‑CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Cap amount and mutuality meet the fallback, but there are no carve‑outs and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes liability for loss of our records/data. Add a mutual "Excluded Claims" § 9.3 (confidentiality/data and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement); cap amount untouched. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment | Restrictions run against us only; IBM may assign freely. Add an affiliate/asset‑sale carve‑out for us and subject IBM's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) with a competitor bar. No change‑of‑control provision exists, so no walk‑away issue. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | Preferred position. No exclusivity, sole‑supplier or requirements obligation; § 14.16 is mutual. No redline. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | § 3.4(b) early termination charges are defined only by cross‑reference to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, with no ceiling. Take the fallback: cap aggregate charges at three months' recurring Charges as our sole liability for the termination. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License | The Base Components licence is expressly "revocable" with no standard, and names Customer only. Add Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf and limit revocation to termination for our uncured material breach. Transferability is already met via § 14.10. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non‑compete on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | Preferred position. § 14.11 (no resale) and § 12.1 (scope of use) are ordinary licence limits, not business restraints. No redline. |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | No usage, licence or fee audit right binds us — better than preferred. Noted for the file only: § 11.3 does not bind investigators to confidentiality or expressly limit access to our systems; we could raise this if the clause opens for other reasons. |
| 10 | Medium | MFN — Most‑favoured‑nation obligations | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | Preferred position. No parity obligation in §§ 4.1, 4.2 or 14.16. No MFN in our favour either, which is an upside item, not a deviation. |
| 11 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | Preferred position. Charges are payable for ordered or actual usage only; § 11.5 imposes no capacity floor. Confirm on diligence that the attachments contain no minimum‑volume or shortfall charge. |
| 12 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non‑solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.8 Personnel | Preferred position. No no‑hire or solicitation covenant anywhere. No redline. |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto‑renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal | 90‑day non‑renewal notice and renewal terms "equal in duration to the previous term" permit automatic multi‑year renewals; no uplift cap. Ask: 12‑month renewals, 30‑day opt‑out, 60‑day reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. Fallback: 60‑day window with 5% cap. |
| 14 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Notice and mutuality meet preferred (we hold the right at one month; IBM has none). The exit is conditioned on uncapped charges with no refund. Cap § 3.4(b) at three months' fees and add pro‑rata refund of prepaid fees; one‑month notice untouched. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post‑termination assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | No transition assistance or Content/data return obligation anywhere; § 3.5 covers accrued payments only. Insert the preferred exit provision (six months' assistance at then‑current rates, machine‑readable return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification), which § 14.2 already preserves. |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Care‑and‑skill warranty only; no conformance warranty, period or remedy, and § 5.4(c) puts all Materials "AS IS" while § 5.2 makes § 5.1 exclusive. Add a 90‑day conformance and no‑malicious‑code warranty for Materials with repair/re‑performance/refund, and carve the express warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer. |
| 17 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York law is our preferred position, but no forum is designated anywhere. Add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County; law unchanged. § 14.4 jury waiver and § 14.14 two‑year limitation are mutual and not flagged. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance clause anywhere, and IBM hosts our environment and processes personal information. Insert new § 14.12A: CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O 1M / cyber 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the positions our playbook treats as walk‑away, and we should not sign without movement on each:

1. **§ 8.2(a)(3) — uncapped Customer indemnity for Services Recipient claims.** An open‑ended indemnity, excluded from our cap by § 9.2(a), for claims "related, directly or indirectly" to IBM's own Services. The partial relief in § 8.2(c) for IBM's misconduct does not cure it. Minimum acceptable outcome: the limb is deleted so our indemnity covers Content/AUP, Customer Components and our breach of applicable law.
2. **§ 3.4(b) / LD — uncapped early termination charges.** A Customer‑payable termination amount with no ceiling, set by cross‑reference to documents not in the reviewed text, could approach or exceed remaining contract value. Minimum acceptable outcome: the three‑month cap (fallback).
3. **§ 12.1 — at‑will revocable licence.** IBM may withdraw the Base Components licence at will, with no stated standard. Minimum acceptable outcome: revocation limited to termination for our uncured material breach.
4. **§ 3.2 — multi‑year automatic renewal.** Renewal terms "equal in duration to the previous term" tied to a 90‑day notice window permit automatic multi‑year lock‑in. Minimum acceptable outcome: the 60‑day / 5% fallback.
5. **§ 5.1 / § 5.4(c) — no conformance warranty with all Materials "AS IS".** This approaches the walk‑away position for deliverables; we need the 90‑day conformance warranty and remedy.
6. **INSURANCE — no coverage from a vendor processing personal data on our behalf.** Absence of any insurance undertaking is walk‑away territory under the rule; the E&O / cyber fallback limits are available.

We note for completeness that the § 9.1/9.2 caps and the IP position in § 7, while critical, are not walk‑away items on their own terms — there is no assignment of our IP or data to IBM and no joint ownership, and the cap is mutual and at the fallback on amount.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the twelve items requiring change: §§ 8.2, 7 (plus a Content/data ownership sentence), new 9.3, 14.10, 3.4(b), 12.1, 3.2, 3.4/T4C refund, 3.5, 5.1/5.4(c), 14.3 and new 14.12A. Every fix is drafted as a minimal, mostly single‑sentence amendment; the cap amount, the one‑month convenience notice, IBM's § 8.1 indemnity and § 14.8 subcontracting are all left untouched.
2. **Request the missing attachments.** Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments are not part of the reviewed document but drive early termination charges (§ 3.4(b)) and pricing (§ 4.1). We need them to confirm there is no minimum‑volume or shortfall charge and to size the exit cost.
3. **Sequence the negotiation.** Lead with the six walk‑away items above; treat the § 7 IP default, the § 9.3 carve‑outs, transition assistance and insurance as the next tier; hold GOVLAW venue and the § 11.3 investigator confidentiality points as low‑cost closing asks.
4. **Business input required on** (a) acceptable renewal uplift if IBM resists the CPI/3% cap, (b) the transition period we need operationally (six months preferred, 90 days at fallback), and (c) whether the three‑month exit cap is affordable against the deal's expected term.
5. **Report back** with IBM's mark‑up against this memo so we can confirm which items have cleared the fallback and which remain live before escalation."}
